messages.subject: Help to start Survey Design
parts:
Hello :)

I wrote some questions in the past in this group, however I created a new topic because I didn't expain quite well what I wanted to do.

So, from the beginning:

I intend to do survey design for marine litter surveys on beaches, using distance sampling along transects. Strip transects will have width of 2,5 m for each side, wchich means 5 m width in total.

I will sample 6 beaches, so for each beach I will have to create a study area (a map, right ?), and I want Distance to give me the best option for the arrangement of transects. I already read the example 3 of user's guide that focus this subject.

First question: 

When preparing the coordinates of the beach (study area), how many vertices are need to create a map of the study area? Can I introduce only 4 vertices creating a rectangle, in which transects will then be placed or the best option (and more correct) is to introduce vertices enough to create a map with the contours of the beach to have a map with an area more similar to the reality?

Second question:

After creating the map of the study area, I will have to create a Coverage Layer with a grid spacing (distance between grid points) approximately equal to the transect strip width (In this case 2,5 m), right?

Then, I'll have to Create a Survey Design and make an Automated Generation of New Survey. Through the Design Statistics, I will choose what is the best design, right?


I apologise if the question are too basic, I am trying to start building projects in Distance.

Thank you in advance!


Sara Sá

messages.author: 9b03386432b784c0
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Help to start Survey Design
parts:
Hi Sara,

The questions you ask are perhaps too much about details - how to implement a design in Distance, when, from your wording, you seem to have trouble with GIS and shapefiles. First you need to think about the big picture.

The most important thing is that you should make sure that your transects are perpendicular to any density gradients that you might expect, so that the usual assumption about sensors being located at random with respect to objects is respected (conversely, if you put transects going along the beach it will, almost for sure, be violated). In a beach, I would say that means that you would ideally have transects perpendicular to the shore line.

I would simply have my transects systematically spaced x meters apart with a random start, with the actual spacing dependent on the available effort. 

If the beach is quite wide and long it might be more efficient to have a zig-zag design. 

Hope this helps,

T

parts:
Hello,

A question arose to me while I was doing the survey design of my marine litter project on the beaches, about which I already posed some questions in this group.

By doing the survey design in Distance, they give me the exact locations of my transects, right? But when I get to the beach I can see that this place will not be good for transects, but another, because strandlines are always changing.

Is it possible for me to do the transects on the beach, in the most suitable places, (registering the GPS positions) and then do a survey design in distance, with the coordinates obtained on the beach? To draw transects in Distance after sampling or that doesn't make sense?

Or do the transects in the most appropriate way on the beach (taking care that the following samplings are done in the same place) and then only do the statistical analysis in Distance with the results obtained and forget the survey design?

There will be, in principle, 5 zigzag transects, each 20 meters in a section of the beach. I send out an outline of the transects I plan to do.

Thank you for the opportunity to share my questions.


Sara Sá

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Help to start Survey Design
parts:
Sara

Survey design is important for ensuring the transects you sample are representative of the area you wish to study.  The key element in survey design is the element of randomness.  We cannot, with our eyes, decide where to place our transects so as to be representative of the study area.

The purpose of the survey design engine is to allow you to define your study region and a few other details, then the software will examine designs within that region consistent with your design specifications.  Having examined the characteristics of the design, you can have the software produce a single realisation of that design that, as you say, specifies the locations of your transects.

It does not make sense to "design" your survey after the sampling has been conducted.

The most delicate part of the question you ask is here "do the transects in the most appropriate way on the beach".  From a statistical perspective "most appropriate way" is defined as *most representative* i.e. being comfortable with the idea that where you did sample resembles where you did not sample.

As we discussed in our earlier correspondence, it is better to have many short transects than few short transects.  The design you provide has but 5 transects, it would be better to have 20 transects.  Hence instead of 5 transects of length 20m, consider having 20 transects of length 5m.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Help to start Survey Design
parts:
Sara

I have now had the term "strand line" defined for me so I appreciate the challenge of them changing.

Perhaps you could employ a design whereby your transects are placed perpendicular to the strand lines and some systematic distance (e.g. 50m or 100m).  You would then sample a transect that runs the width of the strand line.  Your 'study area' would be the strand line.  In addition to your sampling data, you would record the length of each transect.  You could then estimate the density of plastic within the strand line.
